events.text: Your first morning in {sect}. You are woken at the fourth watch, handed a broom, and told that sweeping the thousand steps IS the training.

effects.log: By noon an elder stops to watch you sweep. He says nothing. He comes back the next day.

choices.text: Find a smarter way to sweep

ok.log: You sweep with the wind instead of against it. Half the time, twice as clean. The elders argue about whether to punish you or promote you.

fail.log: Your 'smarter way' involves a donkey. It does not end well for the donkey, or the steps.

events.text: The sect assigns you to escort a merchant caravan through bandit country. Pay: 60 taels and merit points. Risk: bandits, obviously.

ok.log: Two ambushes, zero losses. The merchant tries to marry you to one of his children. You politely flee.

fail.log: You get the caravan through, minus one cart and some of your blood.

effects.log: Dusty scrolls, no bandits. The librarian likes you.

events.text: The stronghold wants you to 'collect a debt' from a salt merchant who stopped paying for protection.

effects.log: He pays. His children watch from the doorway. You tell yourself it is business.

ok.log: You talk him into paying and he thanks you for it. You are good at this. It worries you.

fail.log: He laughs you out of the shop. The stronghold's boss is not amused.

choices.text: Pay it yourself and tell them it is done

effects.log: The merchant never learns why the bandits stopped coming.

events.text: The Cult sends you to test an Orthodox sect's defences: sneak in, leave a black lotus on the sect leader's pillow, and get out.

ok.log: The black lotus is found at dawn. The whole Orthodox Alliance is in uproar. The Cult elders smile at you in the corridor.

fail.log: You are spotted on the roof. You escape with an arrow in your shoulder and nothing to show for it.

effects.log: You leave it on the gatehouse instead. The Cult pretends to be impressed.

events.text: The annual sect tournament. The top three win a spirit elixir and the elders' attention.

ok.log: You take first place. Your name goes up on the sect's wall of honour.

fail.log: You go out in the quarter-finals, with a respectable black eye.

effects.log: You lose in the second round, on purpose, and watch everyone else's techniques very closely.

events.text: You are caught breaking curfew (in your defence, the moon was very nice). The elders sentence you to a month in the punishment cave.

effects.log: Silence, darkness, and bad rice. You come out calmer, and slightly stronger. The moon was still worth it.

events.text: The sect leader summons you. 'Your merit is enough. You may choose one manual from the inner library.'

effects.log: The method is slow, and deep, like a river under ice.
It looks spectacular. Everyone wants to spar with you now.

ok.log: Nobody picks it because nobody can read it. You can. Barely. It is extraordinary.

fail.log: It is a cookbook. A good cookbook.

events.text: {npc} watches you practise for an hour without a word. Then {he} takes your wrist and moves it one finger's width to the left.

choices.text: Practise that finger's width for a month

effects.log: One finger's width. Everything changes.
'Because the sword is not in your hand,' {npc} says, and walks away. You think about it for years.

events.text: Late one night you find {npc} weeping over an old sword. '{His} sect,' {he} says finally. 'Destroyed. I was the only one who ran.'

effects.log: {npc} looks at you a long time. Then {he} teaches you the sect's last technique.

mem.note: sat with me on the worst night

effects.log: Neither of you says anything. It is the most important night of your apprenticeship.

events.text: {npc} does not come out of seclusion. When you open the door, {he} is sitting in meditation, peaceful, gone. A letter is folded in {his} lap.

effects.log: 'You were the best thing I did with my life. The manual under the floor is yours. Do not waste it crying.' You cry anyway.

choices.text: Keep vigil for three days before you read it

effects.log: Three days of incense and silence. When you finally read the letter, you already know what it says: the manual under the floor is yours. Do not waste it crying.

events.text: Your father, {npc}, is getting old. He asks you to come home for the New Year, just once.

mem.note: came home for the New Year

effects.log: He cries when he sees you at the door. You eat too much. It is the best week in years.
You train through the New Year. The letter he sends back is short.

events.text: A letter from {npc}: 'Are you eating? Your cousin became a county clerk. Just saying. The pig says hello.'

effects.log: You read it three times. The pig, you assume, is fine.

events.text: The family elders have arranged a marriage alliance: {npc}, from an allied family. You have met once, at a funeral.

effects.log: The wedding is enormous. Your spouse turns out to have a sharp tongue and a sharper mind. It could be worse.
The elders shout for a week. You have never felt more free.

events.text: Your first child is born in spring. Small, loud, and already trying to grab your sword.

effects.log: You hold your child and, for the first time in your life, the path to the peak does not seem like the most important thing.

events.text: {npc} finds you training at midnight again. 'You are always chasing the next realm. Will you still be here when it matters?'

choices.text: Put the sword down and come to bed

mem.note: put the sword down for me

effects.log: The next realm can wait one night.
It is three more hours. The bed is cold when you get there.

events.text: You hear that {npc} has reached {npc_realm}, ahead of you. At a banquet, {he} raises a cup to you from across the room and smiles.

effects.log: A truce, maybe. Or a promise.
You train until your hands bleed. That smile follows you into every session.

events.text: {npc} is getting married, and wants you to stand beside {him} at the wedding.

mem.note: stood beside me at my wedding

effects.log: You give a speech. It is too long and slightly embarrassing. Everyone cries anyway.
The gift is expensive. {npc} would have preferred you.

events.text: War breaks out between the Orthodox Alliance and the Unorthodox Alliance over a disputed river port. Every martial artist in the province must choose a side, or be chosen.

ok.log: After a season of fighting, you are known on both sides of the river. Some call you a hero. Some call you worse.

fail.log: You are wounded in the first great battle and carried off the field.

choices.text: Protect the villages behind the lines

effects.log: No glory, no songs. Just a lot of villages still standing at the end.
The war ends in a year. Nobody remembers who won. Everybody remembers who hid.

events.text: Rumours spread: the Heavenly Demon has come out of seclusion. Sects are closing their gates. Merchants are raising prices. Someone has painted a black lotus on the town gate.

ok.log: It was a drunk painter's prank. You find him. The whole town laughs for a month, with relief.

fail.log: You follow the trail into the hills and meet something that was definitely not a drunk painter. You run.

choices.text: Go into seclusion until it blows over

effects.log: The rumour fades by winter. You come out stronger, and slightly paranoid.

events.text: You find your first grey hair. Then your second. By evening you have given up counting.

effects.log: Time is the one opponent nobody beats. You might as well get wiser while it wins.

events.text: A young martial artist travels three provinces to ask you one question: 'What is the secret of the martial path?'

effects.log: They look disappointed. In twenty years they will understand.

choices.text: Tell them about your mistakes instead

effects.log: You talk until the tea is cold. It is the best lesson you have ever given.
They bring the chicken. You are becoming your old master. Terrifying.

events.text: You feel the years in your joints. Maybe it is time to see the places you always meant to see.

effects.log: You stand on the shore and watch the sun come up out of the water. You understand something about endless things.

choices.text: Stay and train. There is still time

effects.log: There is never enough time. You train anyway.

events.text: A street vendor swears her dumplings contain the essence of a thousand-year python. They contain pork. Probably.

ok.log: Delicious. If there was a thousand-year python in there, it was a tasty one.

fail.log: Whatever was in dumpling number seven was not pork. You spend two days regretting everything.

effects.log: It is a perfectly normal dumpling. You are almost disappointed.

events.text: You practise your lightness technique across the town rooftops at night and land, with great elegance, in a family's bathtub. They are in it.

effects.log: Very profusely. You offer to pay for the tub. They refuse, which is somehow worse. You never use that street again.

ok.log: Incredibly, they believe you. The legend of the Bathtub Immortal spreads through town.

fail.log: They do not believe you. The grandmother has a very good throwing arm.

events.text: You finally master a technique from a manual bought in the market, and proudly perform it for your friends. It is a dance. For weddings.

effects.log: Surprisingly, it is very popular at weddings. You are invited to eleven this year.

events.text: A goat follows you everywhere for a week, staring at you meaningfully. The villagers say it is the reincarnation of a great master.

effects.log: The goat bows back. Probably. It is hard to tell with goats.

ok.log: The goat leads you to a spring you never knew existed. The water tastes of power.

fail.log: The goat headbutts you and eats your hat. Guidance received.

events.text: You invent your first original technique. It needs a name worthy of the murim.

effects.log: It is a very good punch with a very long name. People shout it when they fight you.
The simplicity terrifies your opponents. What kind of master calls it 'Punch'?

choices.text: Name it after your childhood pig

effects.log: The 'Bao-Bao Strike' becomes surprisingly famous. The pig would be proud.

events.text: Watching rain drip from the eaves, you suddenly understand how energy should flow through the eighth meridian.

effects.log: You sit still until the rain stops, afraid to lose the feeling.

events.text: Your meridians still twist from the qi deviation. Some days you cannot lift a bowl of rice.

effects.log: A year of slow breathing and bitter medicine. The twisting fades.
The cure works instantly. The Cult's envoy smiles. 'We will ask a favour someday.'

events.text: The Cult envoy returns. 'The favour. There is a scroll in the county magistrate's archive. Bring it to us.'

effects.log: You hand over the scroll. You never find out what was in it. You try not to wonder.

ok.log: You fight off the envoy's men. The Cult does not come back. Yet.

fail.log: They leave you for dead in the snow. You are not quite dead.
